sources.title: Saskatchewan has 42 wildfire detection towers, but no AI camera system, SPSA says

notes_for_editor: Built year, builder and reason for the site are not in any source; the Firetowers list and firelookout.ca both leave the year blank or N/A, so no built event is written. Agency: the record says 'formerly Dept. of Natural Resources', which no cached source supports; the Prince Albert Daily Herald (cite 3) covers SPSA's 42 detection towers at network level only and does not name White Fox, so no agency fact is written. Staffing: the record's 'unstaffed' status and its note that Saskatchewan moved to cameras 'from 2013-14' are not supported by any cached source for this tower; the 2013-14 date appears only in the prairies-north survey candidate note. Consider correcting the record's staffing note. Today: the only description of the site is one undated firelookout.ca user submission (submitter QL2C); its present-tense text implies the tower and cabin are still there, but the record's status stays 'unknown' and no status fact is written. The record's 'copula' is read as cupola. Location: the Firetowers DMS 53-34-28.4 X 103-44-03.4 matches the record (53.57456, -103.73428); firelookout.ca gives 53.574164, -103.734552, about 50 m apart; no correction proposed. Two WebSearch-style lookups for the name mostly returned the village of White Fox, which no source ties to this tower, so the village is not used. Canada Lookouts (canada-lookouts.weebly.com) lists White Fox in its index only and is not cited. Valerie Rogers: the Firetowers list prints 'Valerie Rogers - year unknown' after White Fox's NOTES label, before Lockwood Lake; the layout does not show whether this is a towerman or a note (the same name sits under NAMES of TOWERMEN at Grassy Lake), so it is left out of the story.
